source.title: isEmail() returns true for strings containing an email plus extra characters

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
## Describe the problem

The `isEmail()` string extension returns `true` for strings that merely
contain a valid email address plus extra characters. The `EMAIL_REGEXP`
used by `isEmail()` has no `^`/`$` anchors, and the function only
compensates for spaces through an ad-hoc `value.includes(' ')` check.
Any other surrounding characters, such as trailing punctuation, a path
segment, or angle brackets, are silently ignored.

This contradicts the documented behaviour, where
`"It's me@example.com".isEmail()` is documented to return `false`, i.e.
`isEmail()` is meant to answer "is this entire string an email?".

## To reproduce

1. Open any workflow expression field (or a Code node) that supports
   string extensions.
2. Evaluate the following expressions:

   ```js
   "test@example.com!".isEmail()
   "test@example.com;".isEmail()
   "test@example.com/extra".isEmail()
   "<test@example.com>".isEmail()
   ```

   The same result can be observed directly on the extension:

   ```ts
   import { stringExtensions } from '@n8n/expression-runtime';
   const isEmail = stringExtensions.functions.isEmail;
   isEmail('test@example.com!'); // true
   ```

## Expected behavior

All four expressions above should return `false`, matching the
documented `"It's me@example.com".isEmail()` returning `false`. A plain
`"me@example.com".isEmail()` should still return `true`, and
`extractEmail()` should keep extracting an email from a larger sentence.

## Actual behavior

All four expressions above return `true`. Only inputs containing a
space are rejected, so strings with trailing punctuation, appended path
segments or surrounding angle brackets are treated as valid email
addresses.

## Impact

Workflows that use `isEmail()` to validate or route incoming data (form
submissions, webhook payloads, contact imports, conditional branches)
can accept malformed values as valid emails. Invalid addresses may then
be stored, forwarded to downstream services, or used in recipient
fields, and validation becomes inconsistent with `extractEmail()` and
`extractDomain()`.

## Affected code

- `packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts`
  - `EMAIL_REGEXP` (unanchored) and `isEmail()`.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text:
I checked the current implementation: `isEmail()` calls the same unanchored `EMAIL_REGEXP` used by `extractEmail()`, then only rejects values containing a space. That explains why punctuation, path suffixes, and angle brackets can pass while extraction still needs to find an address inside surrounding text.

One way to preserve that extraction behavior is to keep `EMAIL_REGEXP` unchanged and require the `isEmail()` match to cover the whole input (for example, check both `match.index === 0` and `match[0].length === value.length`). That avoids broadening the validation regex while leaving `extractEmail()` unchanged. The existing sentence example and the four reported suffix/prefix cases would be useful regression cases.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: One implementation detail is worth preserving in the fix: `extractEmail()` uses the same unanchored `EMAIL_REGEXP` to find an address inside text, so anchoring that shared regex would change extraction behavior. `isEmail()` can instead require its match to start at index 0 and span the full input (and keep the existing space check); that rejects the reported wrappers/suffixes without changing extraction. The documented sentence example plus the four cases in the report would cover both contracts.
